prompt:
You are a grounded brand-outreach assistant for our team. Use only the evidence passages below.
Never use outside knowledge. Return valid JSON only.

Separate three things:
1. OBSERVED FACTS - things a passage actually states about this company. Each fact is a claim with an id (C1, C2, ...),
   the passage id(s) that support it, and an exact quote copied word-for-word from that passage.
2. UNKNOWNS - things the evidence does not tell us (put them in "unknowns"). A channel, program or audience that does
   not appear in these passages is UNKNOWN. It is never a weakness, never a "gap", and never a reason for outreach.
3. PROPOSALS - collaboration ideas from our team. Proposals are not facts, but each must build on a positively supported
   fact (an existing campaign, partnership, product, community, value or theme) and cite that premise.

Rules:
- Put a claim marker like {C1} (curly braces) right after every factual statement in every field, including the
  email and Instagram idea. Do not write citation numbers yourself; markers are converted to citations later.
- A claim's "quote" must be copied character-for-character from the cited passage: 5 to 25 consecutive words, no
  paraphrasing, no joining of separate sentences. If you cannot find such a quote, drop the claim and every sentence
  that depends on it.
- Audience and strategy sentences are factual: each needs a marker. If no passage states the audience, write
  INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE instead of guessing.
- Pitch lines (email subject, hook, concept) should describe the proposed post ("A carousel featuring ...",
  "Collaborate on ..."). Any statement in them about what the company already does needs a marker.
- Respect passage types. "proposed_or_mock_work" and "author_recommendation" passages describe ideas, not things the
  company did: never state them as company activity. "provider_reported_result" passages are claims by a vendor or
  agency: attribute them ("X reports that ..."). "creator_or_influencer_audience_data" describes creators' followers,
  not the company's customers. "vendor_generated_profile_or_analytics" passages are a tool vendor's estimates
  (e.g. inferred age ranges): attribute them and never present them as the company's own data.
  "forward_looking_statement" passages describe plans or intentions, not completed activity.
- Mind time: if a passage describes past activity, do not present it as current.
- "marketing_gaps" may only contain a weakness that a passage positively states. Usually it is [].
- Never promise results. Describe benefits as goals or possibilities ("could", "aims to"), not guaranteed outcomes.
- Decision: write "draft" when at least one concrete, evidence-supported collaboration opportunity exists. Otherwise write
  "abstain", give an abstain_reason, set pitch fields to INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE and leave collaboration_opportunities empty.
- The email is from our team to the company, proposing one collaborative Instagram post. The pitch, the post idea and
  every collaboration opportunity are for Instagram only (no TikTok, YouTube, podcasts or other channels).
- When a sentence uses a vendor, agency or analytics passage, name that source in the sentence itself
  ("According to AdLibrary, ...", "Attentive reports that ...").
- Each "unknowns" item names one specific thing the passages do not tell us (e.g. "Whether X runs a creator program").
  Never write placeholder text such as "what the evidence does not show".

Required JSON:
{
  "decision": "draft" or "abstain",
  "abstain_reason": "string or empty",
  "claims": [{"id": "C1", "kind": "fact | provider_reported | premise", "statement": "string",
              "passage_ids": ["P1"], "quote": "exact words from the passage"}],
  "brand_summary": "Full sentences, each followed by its marker, e.g. "X makes ... {C1}." Never only markers. Or INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE",
  "likely_target_audience": "A full sentence followed by its marker, or INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE",
  "current_marketing_strategy": ["text with markers"],
  "unknowns": ["one specific open question, e.g. Whether the company works with creators"],
  "marketing_gaps": [],
  "collaboration_opportunities": ["proposal that builds on a cited fact {C2}"],
  "instagram_post_idea": {"hook": "string", "concept": "string", "why_it_fits": "string"},
  "email_subject": "string",
  "email_body": "string"
}

Recipient: the marketing team

[P2] source: https://adlibrary.com/brands/momofuku-goods | document: third_party_confirmed | type: provider_reported_result | flags: vendor_generated_profile_or_analytics | dates in text: none | published: unknown
"Momofuku Goods Meta Ads (Facebook & Instagram): Platform Analysis Momofuku Goods' social advertising features chef-level food photography alongside recipe tutorials that showcase the products in restaurant-quality applications. [P3] source: https://adlibrary.com/brands/momofuku-goods | document: third_party_confirmed | type: provider_reported_result | flags: vendor_generated_profile_or_analytics | dates in text: none | published: unknown
"Momofuku Goods Google Ads, YouTube Ads & Cross-Platform Lessons Momofuku Goods demonstrates the value of extending a trust-credentialed brand into new product categories rather than building brand trust from scratch. For operators with strong brand equity: product line extensions into pantry and consumer goods can generate revenue with significantly lower marketing investment than new brand creation."

[P4] source: https://archive.com/customer-stories/momofuku-goods | document: third_party_confirmed | type: descriptive | dates in text: none | published: unknown
"The Results Archive has given Kyle and the team the in-depth visibility they always wanted. For example, Momofuku killed it on social last summer. Going viral on TikTok pushed impressions to all-time highs, which coincided with some of the brand's biggest sales months. Connecting the dots to specific campaigns was easy with Archive. ‍ Now Kyle can draw a definitive line between specific seeding campaigns and increased brand awareness, traffic, or revenue. ‍ While impressions are important to Momofuku Goods, so are their sources."

[P5] source: https://adlibrary.com/brands/momofuku-goods | document: third_party_confirmed | type: provider_reported_result | flags: vendor_generated_profile_or_analytics | dates in text: 2020 | published: unknown
"About Momofuku Goods Momofuku Goods launched in 2020 as the consumer product extension of David Chang's Momofuku restaurant group. The brand sells chili crisp, seasoned salts, soy sauce, and noodles via DTC and major retail, leveraging Chang's enormous culinary celebrity and the Momofuku restaurant brand's cultural cachet to compete in the premium condiment and specialty pantry category. Also searched as Momofuku."

[P6] source: https://archive.com/customer-stories/momofuku-goods | document: third_party_confirmed | type: descriptive | dates in text: none | published: unknown
"The Challenge Every month, Momofuku Goods seeds product to influencers hoping to develop organic relationships and generate awareness as efficiently as possible. ‍ But Kyle didn’t have a good way to measure how the program was doing. He also didn’t have the data to intelligently allocate resources or adapt his tactics. > “In CPG, the name of the game is brand awareness, not conversion. We are trying to find new > channels to drive awareness efficiently at scale."

[P7] source: https://www.reacherapp.com/customers/momofuku | document: third_party_confirmed | type: descriptive | dates in text: none | published: unknown
"Cohort analysis Monthly cohort reports breaking down every creator activated, videos posted, and views generated. Lets Momofuku see if reactivation efforts are actually improving performance within cohorts over time."

[P8] source: https://www.reacherapp.com/customers/momofuku | document: third_party_confirmed | type: descriptive | flags: creator_or_influencer_audience_data | dates in text: none | published: unknown
"Campaign-driven allocation Strategy pivots based on upcoming campaigns. For the April viral recipe challenge, Reacher shifted 150 samples into Chili Crunch because it consistently outperforms, instead of splitting evenly across products. > 150 samples reallocated to Chili Crunch. Strategy pivots based on campaigns, product performance, > and earned media goals, not fixed splits. The Result Reacher Plus took Momofuku's creator program from a capacity-limited internal build to a tailored operation that measures what Momofuku actually cares about: earned media value, impressions, and CPM per sample."

[P9] source: https://www.reacherapp.com/customers/momofuku | document: third_party_confirmed | type: provider_reported_result | flags: creator_or_influencer_audience_data | dates in text: none | published: unknown
"2.4× sample requests month over month (458 in February to 1,100 in March) * 100% more videos posted (in March vs. prior month) * Custom EMV and CPM reporting (built around Momofuku's specific KPIs) * Monthly cohort analysis (creator activation, videos, view generation over time) * 150 samples reallocated to Chili Crunch (ahead of April viral recipe campaign)"
